This one's a tough call. It's a fun and satisfying action game, and even better for a WH40K fan. But since it's mostly a single player experience these days, I don't find that the price is justifiable for the length of the campaign (about 6-7 hours on normal). The game is sweet, but short. That said, I've enjoyed a playthrough on harder difficulty too.

EDIT: I thought the Ork machine in the promo pictures didn't appear in the game, but I've been informed it's in the online play DLC which I do not own. So if you invest in the DLC and play online (probably best with friends so you can set up a co-op game easily) you'll see it!

I snagged this one during a fire sale for a few bucks, so I felt far less bad about quitting the SP campaign out of boredom after a few hours. I'm not exactly steeped in the lore of the Warhammer universe, so perhaps there are subtleties that I missed here that would have changed my perception for the better, but the story and its characters always felt dull and flat to me. I can usually forgive a game like this a lackluster story if combat is fun and engaging enough, but unfortunately that wasn’t the case. There was some mechanical satisfaction with things like the jet pack, but beyond that movement and most of the game’s pitched battles felt clunky and unsatisfying to me. Maybe this was all a far more impressive package back when it came out?

YMMV, but I’d say pass unless A) you’re already a serious fan of the mythos, and B) it’s on sale.

It doesn't really do anything new, but honestly, when I played it I simply didn't care. Had a blast with the campaign and am currently shreading friends in multiplayer (exterminatus is cool too). The combat is very satisfying, especially melee and the gorey executions.

And it's 40k so automatic +rep for this one! [spoiler]Ending is complete ♥♥♥♥ though...[/spoiler]

Warhammer 40K: Space Marine is one of the better Warhammer games out there because of a couple of reasons:

First: Games Workshop sometimes is very generous to whom they give the license to make games, because of this, there's a lot of Warhammer games that are either forgettable or don't have good quality.

Second: Warhammer 40K has a long history with games, PC specifically like the Space Hulk franchise, but most games were designed with the idea of also letting you play with other races besides the space marines so they have to balance the factions to not feel as overpowered or they just ramped the difficulty making your units feel like they were made of paper, like early Space Hulk games.

Space Marine not only has the quality of a Triple A game in all the right places made by a studio that actually cared for the product but also lets you play a complete campaing as a space marine so you can really go all out and its one of the most accurate representations of what a space marine can do. 

The soundtrack is orchestra, very well composed but it makes you miss some of the chants other games have for the space marine chapters.

The story is also a good selling point if you dont't know much about the warhammer universe or if this is your first contact with the franchise, the lore is massive with a great amount of backstory, worlds, space marine chapters and alien races but they're not required in order to enjoy this game, the story is straightforward and easy to follow with characters just mentioning lore from the side, a good entry point for the Warhammer universe.

The gameplay as I said before, its the strongest point of the game, not being tied to any other race to balance for the single player story lets you have full control of a captain space marine, the weapons in the warhammer universe range from brutal to overpowered, and this game does them great justice, all of them feeling incredible to handle. The game gives you the option to play ranged or melee, some guns are more powerful than others but all of them are viable to finish the game. There is no cover system in the game which is good, you're a space marine, you don't need one, but I do recommend to play the game in a moderate difficult, higher difficulties will limit you from the melee aspect of the game the closer you are to the endgame because of how accurate the enemies are and some levels will become a spamfest, making you try to take cover when the game wasn't designed for it.

The game also has 2 multiplayer modes, a 8v8 that is dead for the most part so don't count on it, and a horde mode that still works since you can use P2P to play with your friends, but if you want to play co-op warhammer games with your friends there are better options like Eternal Crusade or the most recent Space Hulk games, so you'll want to get this game for its most important aspect, the single player campaing, best option would be to wait for a sale to get it.

One of the weak aspects of the game is the scenary and the backgrounds, the explanation for this is that the world the story takes place is a forge world (basically the planet being an entire military factory) but this doesn't stop the game's locations from looking the same, the good thing about this is that by making the backgrounds empty for the most part it enhances the performance, so this game can easily reach 60fps as long as your hardware is close to this current decade.

One more thing, this game belongs to the last generation of consoles so there will be quick time events in some moments of the game, nothing too serious.
